eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article addresses automated environmental regulatory compliance monitoring with IoT and open government data; it does not study LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper strongly addresses regulatory compliance, government monitoring, and risk in a regulated environmental domain, the provided text contains no LLM, generative AI, or conversational AI focus. Machine learning is mentioned only as a possible future module in IoT data pipelines, not as the core object of study. The work is therefore outside the review scope on conversational governance in LLM-based systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Exclusion is clear from title, abstract, introduction, and technology description; no conversational or LLM governance content is present in the supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on the limited front-matter text provided. The study appears methodologically coherent for an IoT compliance monitoring application, but ethics, limitations, and detailed analytic procedures are not evidenced in the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: Confidence in the article's own technical claims is moderate within its IoT compliance domain, but relevance to conversational governance in LLM systems is very low because the supplied text does not address LLMs, conversational interfaces, or AI governance mechanisms applicable to language-model systems.

concepts: Internet of Open Government Data and Things

synthesis.main_claim: IoT-generated open government data can be repurposed to build a scalable automated system for environmental flows regulatory compliance monitoring and evaluation at national scale.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes and demonstrates an IoT-based compliance evaluation approach using routinely collected river monitoring data, illustrated with Estonia's national river monitoring network.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence because it does not address conversational AI or LLM governance; it may serve only as distant contextual background on generic regulatory compliance automation outside language-model systems.
